chunks: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Jarir and al-Hasan b. Urwa and Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Wahbi narrated to us. They said: Muhammad b. Humayd narrated to us. He said: Zafir b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Uyayna narrated to us from Abu Hazim from Sahl b. Sa'd. He said:

Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Muhammad! Live for as long as you wish, for indeed you will die. Love whomever you wish, for indeed you will be separated from him. Do whatever you wish, for indeed you will be recompensed for it. And know that the honour of a man is his standing in prayer at night, and his glory is his independence from the people.
ai.seo_question: What did Gabriel say to the Prophet Muhammad about the honour of a man?
ai.summary: The Angel Gabriel delivers a concise and powerful sermon to the Prophet Muhammad, consisting of three parallel admonitions: life ends in death, love ends in separation, and deeds will be requited. He then reveals two markers of true nobility: night prayer and self-sufficiency from people. This hadith is widely transmitted and considered one of the most eloquent prophetic counsels in Islamic literature.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Jarir and al-Hasan b. `Urwa and `Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Wahbi narrated to us. They said: Muhammad b. Humayd narrated to us. He said: Zafir b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Uyayna narrated to us from Abi Hazim from Sahl b. Sa`d.  He said: Gabriel (as) came to the Prophet (s) and said: O Muhammad! Live for as long as you want – you will die. Love whoever you want – you will be separated. Do what you want – you will reap its outcome. Know that the honour of a man is in standing in prayer at night, and his glory is in being needless of the people.
